implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: require a strictly positive integer with no leading zeros (except the literal value itself never being 0) and no sign/whitespace; anything else (e.g. "01", "+1", "1.0", "-1") is treated as a non-matching id and returns 404
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says '<id> that is not a positive integer' -> 404; leading-zero strings like "01" are ambiguous, so I chose the stricter canonical-integer-string reading to avoid two different string ids mapping to the same numeric id

unresolved_intent.decision: split the path on '/' and drop empty segments, so "/items/" normalizes to ["items"] (same as "/items") and "//items" also normalizes to ["items"]
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec never defines trailing-slash or doubled-slash behavior; treating them as equivalent to the canonical path is the least surprising choice and avoids spurious 404s for cosmetic path variants

unresolved_intent.ir_region: non-object items in the top-level request array
unresolved_intent.decision: if the input is a JSON array but any element is not itself a JSON object, the whole run prints exactly ERROR (not a per-element 400)
unresolved_intent.rationale: the contract defines ERROR as the response to input that is not a JSON array of request objects; a non-object element breaks that shape at the array level, distinct from a well-formed request object with a bad body (which does get a 400)

unresolved_intent.ir_region: request object missing 'method' or 'path', or with wrong types for them
unresolved_intent.decision: treat as a per-request 400 {"error": "bad request"} rather than aborting the whole batch with ERROR
unresolved_intent.rationale: ERROR is reserved for the top-level shape (array of objects); once an element is a dict, malformed routing fields are closer to 'bad request' than to a batch-level parse failure, and this keeps 'one bad request does not abort the batch' meaningful for malformed requests too

unresolved_intent.ir_region: body field present but not required for GET/DELETE
unresolved_intent.decision: ignore any 'body' value on GET/DELETE requests entirely (no validation, no error) since only POST/PUT define body requirements
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec's body-validation rule (400 on missing/non-object/no-name-string) is scoped explicitly to POST /items and PUT /items/<id>; extending it to GET/DELETE isn't specified and would invent a new error path

compilation_report.constraint_handling: r2: second blind run of the same model on the same canonical package (ADR-027 intra-model variance)
